title: Gang Busters
paragraphs: Phillips H. Lord true-crime dramatization series built from actual law-enforcement cases, wanted-person bulletins and police/federal cooperation. Frozen GRH snapshot has 88 numbered recordings from 1940-1955.

GRH documents the program through G-Men precursor (July 20, 1935 to October 12, 1935) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], CBS Gang Busters launch era (January 15, 1936 to June 15, 1940) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], Blue Network era (October 11, 1940 to 1945) on [[org|org.acb290b0843b31ec|Blue Network]], and ABC era (1945 to December 25, 1948) on [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Phillips H. Lord (producer on 38 recordings, creator on 2 recordings, and executive producer on 1 recording), Stanley Niss (writer on 27 recordings and director on 4 recordings), Don Gardiner (announcer on 22 recordings), William Sweets (director on 18 recordings and producer on 1 recording), Leonard L. Bass (director on 15 recordings), Frank Readick (performer on 9 recordings), and Gaylord Avery (announcer on 9 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network), [[org|org.244a08401c2c9142|WRVR-FM]] (originated at station), [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] (broadcast on network), and [[org|org.acb290b0843b31ec|Blue Network]] (broadcast on network).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include organized criminal gangs, robbery and burglary, murder and homicide, wanted fugitives, prisons and escapes, and law enforcement investigation.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including True-crime radio and public confidence in law enforcement, Citizen-detective wanted-person bulletins, Gang Busters sound-effects opening and popular phrase, and 1930s gangster and G-man popular culture.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|x-minus-one|X Minus One]] (27 shared credited people), [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]] (29 shared credited people), [[show|columbia-workshop|Columbia Workshop]] (28 shared credited people), [[show|the-mysterious-traveler|The Mysterious Traveler]] (25 shared credited people), and [[show|words-at-war|Words at War]] (25 shared credited people).
